minutes.headline: Water commissioners agreed to ask the Planning Board to replace special permits with site plan review in the water supply zone bylaw.
minutes.summary: The commissioners spent most of the meeting on the town's proposed water supply zone bylaw. They settled on edits to send back to the Planning Board before its 26th meeting. The superintendent also reported on the Mass Ave temporary lines, failed radios and a possible joint radio system, and a Townsend offer. The board decided to reinvest a maturing investment for 12 months. A resident asked about the clean water SRF application and the pilot test at the Keyes well.

public_comment.topic: Supported replacing special permit with site plan review in Zone 1 and 2. Recommended adding the 310 CMR 22 permitted-use language. Explained that the AG reviews a bylaw only after town meeting.
Asked about the passive recreation definition in the bylaw (walking, hiking, skiing, bicycling) and what was decided on it.
Asked whether the district has submitted anything to the state clean water SRF this year. Asked for a status on the pilot test and for the Lancaster Rd past (PFAS) test data.

votes.motion: Roll over or reinvest the maturing investment for 12 months

budget_items.topic: Directional drill extension on Mass Ave project
budget_items.what_was_said: The engineer said going a little further past a driveway would add a modest cost. The board was told it would be an expense to the district.

budget_items.topic: Two-way radio replacement and joint system with fire and police
budget_items.what_was_said: The district's radios are 14-15 years old and failing. The superintendent suggested joining the fire and police upgrade with a combiner antenna, which would split the cost across three departments and help with bidding-law limits.

budget_items.topic: Townsend offer to sell water to Lunenburg Water District
budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed buying or selling water. Past experience was that buying from an outside entity cost more than the loan payment for own supply.
The investment comes due on the 22nd. The money was allocated for the tank. Six- and 12-month rates were offered, and the board favored 12 months given falling rates.

decisions.decision: Commissioners want the special permit requirement removed from Zone 1 and Zone 2 uses, and the H6 item under permitted uses removed.
Instead of deleting the section, the draft will say uses require site plan review where it now says special permit. The Planning Board can accept or not.
The clerk will add the 310 CMR 22 permitted-use language to the draft, highlight the requested changes, and send it back to the Planning Board before its meeting on the 26th.
Once the Planning Board's final version exists, the commissioners will consider forwarding it to DEP for review.
The commissioners favor reinvesting the maturing investment for one year, and the clerk will contact the broker.
The board will post a visit to Townsend's new treatment plant as a full-board meeting after it comes online in mid-September.
The clerk will share the Lancaster Rd past test data with the resident.

The clerk will add the state drinking water permitted-use language, highlight the requested changes, and return the draft before the Planning Board meets on the 26th.
The commissioners favored reinvesting a maturing investment for one year; the clerk will contact the broker. The vote as heard was not audible.
The superintendent reported on failing two-way radios and a possible joint system with fire and police, and on a Townsend offer to sell water.
A resident asked about a state clean water loan application and the Keyes well pilot test; the clerk will share past Lancaster Rd test data.

why_it_matters: The bylaw draft decides whether land uses in the water supply protection zones need a special permit or site plan review, which affects what can be built near the town's wells and what a town meeting vote will be asked to approve.
Replacing aging radios and buying water from a neighbor are costs that could reach water rates, and the minutes record no decision on either.
